one_liner: Supervise a team of program analysts at NAVSEA, overseeing acquisition, cost, schedule and funding execution for complex naval and defense programs at senior (GS-14 equivalent) level.
fit_summary: This supervisory NH-4 role requires a year of GS-13-equivalent experience leading acquisition, contracting, or financial execution for complex defense or naval technical programs. Daniel's emergency-management consulting at IEM and policy knowledge don't map directly to shipbuilding or defense acquisition, and nothing on file shows supervisory or senior program-management experience. Unless Daniel's IEM work involved managing large federal contracts, task orders, or funding lines at a senior level, Daniel likely won't qualify.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens), so no federal status is needed, but this is a flyer for anticipated vacancies: you must follow its How to Apply instructions, and there may be no actual hires.

At least one year of specialized experience equivalent to NH-03/GS-13 leading acquisition, program-management, contracting, procurement, or financial-execution work for complex defense, naval, or similarly technical programs.
Must be able to obtain and keep a Secret security clearance.
Supervisory position: expect to need evidence of leading teams or supervising staff.
keywords: cost, schedule, funding, and contract-performance risks
strategy: Before investing time, honestly check whether your IEM work included managing federal contract task orders, funding lines, deliverables, or budgets at a senior level. If it didn't, prioritize GS-0343 analyst roles at GS-9 to GS-12, especially at FEMA or DHS, where your background is a closer match.
If you apply, frame IEM work as government-contract program execution: name the client agencies, contract or task-order scale, deliverables, schedules, and any budget or burn-rate tracking you did.
Argue the "similarly technical programs" clause only if it's true, such as large federal disaster-recovery grant or contract programs with complex cost and schedule management.
Keep to two pages, and list hours per week, start and end dates (month/year), and supervisory duties for each job so HR can measure your year of specialized experience.
The posting window is October 30 to November 9, 2026, and the flyer itself takes no applications, so read and follow the How to Apply section exactly and early.
resume_bullets: Managed [number] task orders/work packages valued at [$amount] for [federal client agency], tracking deliverables, schedule, and burn rate and reporting status to [client/senior leadership].
Led a cross-functional team of [number] staff supporting [disaster recovery/preparedness program], setting priorities, assigning work, and reviewing quality of deliverables.
Analyzed cost, schedule, and funding risks for [program] and recommended [specific action] to [client leadership], resulting in [verifiable outcome].
interview_questions: Describe a time you managed contract or funding execution on a complex program and spotted a cost or schedule risk early.
How have you supervised or led staff, including handling a performance problem?
Walk us through how you'd evaluate a program's effectiveness across its lifecycle.
How do you build working relationships with contracting, financial, and technical stakeholders who have competing priorities?
watch_outs: The specialized-experience requirement (defense or naval acquisition at GS-13 level, plus supervision) is likely beyond Daniel's documented background, so overstating it risks an ineligible finding.
This is a notice flyer for anticipated vacancies, not a guaranteed job, and no result letters will be sent.
A Secret clearance is required, and on-site work at the Washington Navy Yard means a long commute from Manassas on non-telework days.
